terminal_help_desc: Work through these steps in order. Each one rules out a common cause.
terminal_help_cable_body: Many USB-C and micro-USB cables are charge-only and don't carry data. Swap to a known-good data cable (one you've used to transfer files or connect other devices) and reconnect the hub.
terminal_help_port_body: Plug the device directly into a USB port on your computer. Avoid USB hubs, docking stations, and front-panel ports if possible; these are common sources of power and signal issues. If you're on a desktop, try a port on the back of the machine.
terminal_help_driver_extract: Extract the contents of the zip file to a folder on your computer.
terminal_help_driver_run: Open the folder and run {#code}CP210xVCPInstaller_x64.exe{/code}. Follow the prompts to install.
terminal_help_manual_intro: If the driver installer ran but the device still doesn't show up:
terminal_help_manual_open: Open Device Manager (press {#key}Win{/key} + {#key}X{/key} and select {#code}Device Manager{/code}).
terminal_help_manual_ports: Under {#code}Ports (COM & LPT){/code}, look for an entry like:
terminal_help_manual_missing: If it's missing, the device isn't being detected by Windows at all; revisit the cable and port steps.
terminal_help_manual_update: Right-click the device and pick {#code}Update Driver{/code}.
terminal_help_manual_browse: Choose {#code}Browse my computer for drivers{/code} and select the folder you extracted the driver zip into. Make sure {#code}Include subfolders{/code} is checked.
terminal_help_manual_success: On success, the entry should now read {#code}Silicon Labs CP210x USB to UART Bridge{/code}.
terminal_help_discord_intro: Still stuck after all of the above? Hop into our Discord server and ask in the {#code}# 💭┃support-chat{/code} channel. Please include:
terminal_help_discord_device: the device you're using (board model, where you got it)
terminal_help_discord_tried: what you've already tried from the previous steps
terminal_help_discord_errors: any error messages or relevant terminal output

terminal_cfg_intro: Values are sent to the device via UART. Read the device's response in the console below. Commands without an argument act as getters; use the {#eye/} button next to each field to read the current value.
